strikePaths.name: Community Standards
strikePaths.triggers: Nudity, violence, hateful conduct and harassment, dangerous organizations, self-injury, spam.
strikePaths.escalation: Post removal → temporary limits on posting or Live → blocking or deactivation for repeat and severe cases.
strikePaths.response: Stop the risk, edit similar posts, appeal, and run a clean 90-day plan.

strikePaths.name: Ads Policies
strikePaths.triggers: Misleading claims, landing pages that do not match the ad, personal attributes, circumvention attempts.
strikePaths.escalation: Disapproved ads → limited delivery → restricted ad account → restricted Business Manager.
strikePaths.response: Audit the ads, fix creative, copy, landing page and targeting, then appeal.

strikePaths.name: Monetization
strikePaths.triggers: Brand-safety breaches, missing paid-partnership labels, sensitive topics handled in the wrong tone.
strikePaths.escalation: Limited tools → suspension → removal from the program.
strikePaths.response: Remove the cause, set internal rules for the team, reapply after the waiting period.

strikePaths.name: Copyright and trademarks
strikePaths.triggers: Unlicensed music, video, photos or logos; improper use of a trademark.
strikePaths.escalation: Removal on a rights holder's claim → broader account limits if it repeats.
strikePaths.response: License or replace the asset; file a counter-notice only for a clear error.

sanctions.title: Content removal
sanctions.summary: The post is taken down and the violation stays on the account's record.
sanctions.looksLike: A post, story or reel disappears and you get a notice naming the rule you broke.
sanctions.causes: A Community Standards violation: nudity, violence, hateful conduct, dangerous organizations, self-injury.
firstSteps: Screenshot the notification and save the link to the post.
Read the specific rule that is cited, not the general policy.
Review your similar posts and fix the same problem there.
Appeal only if you have an argument on the merits, not because you disagree.

sanctions.title: Demotion (reduced distribution)
sanctions.summary: The content stays online, but the platform stops showing it widely.
sanctions.looksLike: A sharp drop in reach and in impressions from Discovery, sometimes with a 'sensitive' or 'missing context' label.
sanctions.causes: A risky topic, clickbait, thin context, a misleading thumbnail or hashtags.
firstSteps: Add context and sources to the post.
Replace the thumbnail and headline with neutral ones.
Pause that content series for one to two weeks.
Track whether reach recovers before you post on the topic again.

sanctions.title: Labels and warnings
sanctions.summary: The post gets a label that everyone who sees it sees too.
sanctions.looksLike: 'False', 'partly false', 'missing context', 'altered' or 'sensitive' appears on the post.
sanctions.whereToSee: On the post itself and in your notifications.
sanctions.causes: Missing context, unverified claims, a manipulated visual.
firstSteps: Read the fact-checker's analysis, not just the label.
Add sources and clarifications to the text.
Edit the visual if that is what triggered the label.
Appeal if the review got the facts of your case wrong.

sanctions.title: Feature limits
sanctions.summary: The account works, but specific actions are switched off for a set period.
sanctions.looksLike: A temporary block on posting, comments, messages, Live, groups or Marketplace.
sanctions.causes: Accumulated violations or a single incident, such as graphic footage during a Live.
firstSteps: Stop the activity that caused the limit — continuing extends it.
Plan 90 days without risky posts on the same topic.
Tighten moderation of comments and messages.
Appeal if the limit came from someone else's post or from an error.

sanctions.title: Removed from recommendations
sanctions.summary: What people call a shadowban: the profile stops reaching anyone new.
sanctions.looksLike: Content no longer appears in Explore, recommendations, search or hashtags, and reach falls back to your followers.
sanctions.whereToSee: Account or Page Quality — platforms spell it out as 'Removed from recommendations'.
sanctions.causes: Low quality, repeated reports, borderline topics, earlier warnings.
firstSteps: Check Account Quality before assuming it is a shadowban.
Remove or edit the content flagged as violating.
Publish consistent quality for 30 to 90 days.
Cut back on risky topics until the status clears.

sanctions.title: Temporary account block
sanctions.summary: Access is suspended for a set period, but the profile still exists.
sanctions.looksLike: You cannot log in or act; the screen shows a deadline or an identity check.
sanctions.whereToSee: At login and in the email tied to the profile.
sanctions.causes: Systematic violations or a signal of suspicious activity.
firstSteps: Confirm your identity through the official flow, never through a link in a message.
Change the password and turn on two-factor authentication.
End active sessions on devices you do not recognize.
Appeal if the block came without a violation on your side.

sanctions.title: Disabled or deleted account
sanctions.summary: The heaviest measure: full loss of access, with a deadline for appealing.
sanctions.looksLike: The profile or page will not open; login shows a deactivation message.
sanctions.whereToSee: At login and in the platform's email notifications.
sanctions.causes: Severe or repeated violations, or evading measures already imposed.
firstSteps: Act immediately — the appeal window starts running from the notification.
Collect proof of ownership: documents, old posts, ad invoices.
File an appeal with a specific argument, not a general plea.
Check what archive of your content you hold outside the platform.

sanctions.title: Disapproved ad
sanctions.summary: A single ad is rejected; a series of rejections leads to account-level measures.
sanctions.looksLike: The ad or ad set sits as Disapproved and never starts delivering.
sanctions.causes: A broken ads policy, a landing page that does not match the offer, prohibited claims or targeting.
firstSteps: Read which policy is cited and open it in the help center.
Check all four elements together: creative, copy, landing page and targeting.
Fix it on the merits — swapping one word counts as circumvention.
Appeal with a short note on exactly what you changed.

sanctions.title: Restricted ad account or Business
sanctions.summary: Advertising stops completely — the most expensive sanction for a business.
sanctions.looksLike: You cannot run ads; a restriction appears in Business Settings.
sanctions.causes: Circumvention attempts, sensitive categories, a run of rejections, poor Business Manager hygiene.
firstSteps: Stop uploading new ads until the cause is identified.
Run a full audit: creatives, catalogs, domains, pixels and forms.
Review roles and access and turn on two-factor authentication.
Appeal with evidence of the fixes, and apply Special Ad Categories if they apply to you.

sanctions.title: Suspended or limited monetization
sanctions.summary: The content stays up, but the revenue from it stops.
sanctions.looksLike: Stars, subscriptions or in-stream ads are suspended or limited.
sanctions.causes: Brand-safety breaches, missing paid-partnership labels, sensitive topics in the wrong tone.
firstSteps: Remove the specific content named as the cause.
Set a team rule on who labels partnerships and how.
Wait out the stated period before requesting another review.
Request the review with a description of what changed editorially.

sanctions.title: Copyright and trademarks
sanctions.summary: Removal on a rights holder's claim; repetition brings broader limits.
sanctions.looksLike: Content is taken down on a claim, and some systems also record a strike.
sanctions.whereToSee: The rights section or your Support Inbox.
sanctions.causes: Unlicensed music, video, photos or logos; improper use of a trademark.
firstSteps: Replace the asset or secure a license before re-uploading.
Gather the proof of your right to use it.
File a counter-notice only for a clear error, with documents.
Search your archive for the same asset in older posts.

sanctions.title: Verification removed
sanctions.summary: The badge is gone, and with it part of your credibility and support access.
sanctions.looksLike: The badge disappears from the profile, usually with a short notice.
sanctions.causes: Violations, suspicious activity, changes in the platform's criteria.
firstSteps: Clear the active violations on the account.
Keep the content stable for a few months.
Check whether the profile still meets the current criteria.
Reapply once the record is clean.

statusPlaces.name: Account, Page or Professional Dashboard
statusPlaces.detail: The status section lists removed posts, warnings and whether the profile is out of recommendations.

statusPlaces.name: Support Inbox and notifications
statusPlaces.detail: Official messages about measures and the replies to your appeals land here.

statusPlaces.name: Ads Manager → Account Quality
statusPlaces.detail: Rejections, delivery limits and the state of the ad account.

statusPlaces.name: Monetization Manager
statusPlaces.detail: Warnings and eligibility for the revenue tools.

statusPlaces.name: The rights section
statusPlaces.detail: The history of rights-holder claims and the counter-notices you filed.

reportOutcomes: No action, if the review finds no violation.
Soft measures: demotion and temporarily limited recommendations, comments or sharing.
Temporary removal or a hold on visibility until a moderator reviews it.
Permanent removal and a strike, if a violation is confirmed.
reportSignals: A sudden spike in reports and hostile comments in a short window.
Many new or recently created profiles in the comments.
Calls to 'report this' in outside groups and channels.
Near-identical wording across the reports and comments.

reportSop.title: Collect evidence
reportSop.detail: Screenshots of the calls to mass-report, links, date and time. This is the foundation of any later appeal.

reportSop.title: Tighten safety settings
reportSop.detail: Limit comments to followers, turn on offensive-word filters, restrict tagging where needed.

reportSop.title: Add context to the post
reportSop.detail: A clarification, a source or a warning on sensitive topics; a more neutral thumbnail and description.

reportSop.title: Moderate actively
reportSop.detail: Hide the repeat hostile comments and block the profiles that break the rules.

reportSop.title: Appeal if it comes down
reportSop.detail: Attach the evidence of coordination, the context and the corrections you already made.

reportSop.title: Watch for 90 days
reportSop.detail: Track repeats and schedule risky topics for calmer periods.

myths.myth: Enough reports automatically take a post down.
myths.reality: Reports trigger a review, not a verdict. In sensitive categories a temporary measure is possible, and it can be appealed.

myths.myth: Nothing can be done about coordinated reporting.
myths.reality: There is: protective settings, evidence of the coordination, content fixes, an appeal, and escalation through business support if you have access to it.

myths.myth: A shadowban is a separate sanction.
myths.reality: In most cases it is demotion or removal from recommendations. Both are visible in Account Quality instead of being guessed from your reach.
